newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Egypt's input in peace talks irritates U.S.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's input in peace talks irritates U.S.

text.p: Egypt's input into Israeli-PLO peace talks to clinch a long-delayed deal on the handover of the West Bank city of Hebron to the Palestinians has raised U.S. and Israeli ire, PLO and Israeli officials said on Tuesday.

PLO officials said they were informed by U.S. officials in Jerusalem and Tel Aviv of American anger and objections to the Egyptian role in the Israeli-PLO talks. They quoted them as saying anything beyond a "general contribution" on Egypt's part would only complicate matters.
Israeli officials also criticised Egypt's role in the talks saying it was only complicating the negotiating process.

"The U.S. was angered by Egypt for trying to mediate between the PLO and Israel at the time the U.S. was directly involved in the talks from the start," said a PLO official who refused to be identified.

The official said the United States was also angered when the Palestinians introduced major amendments to an American document which included proposals that could serve as a basis for a Hebron agreement.
Israel was to have withdrawn its troops from Hebron in March under a deal signed more than a year ago.

But Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, elected in May, delayed implementation of the accord, signed by the previous government, demanding increased security for the 400 settlers who live in the city amongst more than 100,000 Palestinians.

"After amending the document Palestinians consulted with Egypt on the amendments and Egypt's Foreign Minister Amr Moussa was expected to visit (Palestinian) self-rule areas and Israel to mediate a deal which further angered the Americans," the Palestinian official said.

The United States was directly involved in mediation efforts between Israel and the PLO in talks on Hebron which began in September. U.S. Middle East peace coordinator Dennis Ross spent six weeks in the region at the time of the Hebron talks.
Ross together with U.S. general Consul in East Jerusalem Edward Abington and American ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk failed to close gaps between the sides.
A senior Israeli official, who requested anonymity said: "In light of the situation, the Americans have intervened and relayed to Egypt how serious the situation would be."
"Instead of coordinating, the Egyptians have entered the talks almost as though they are a side in the negotiations," the official added.
He said a planned visit by Moussa to mediate a Hebron deal "will only complicate the process."
The Israeli official said Egypt's stance, which Israel considers as biased towards the Palestinians, "could bring not only a situation of tension but also confrontation with Egypt."
PLO officials said Washington was applying pressure on the Palestinians instead of taking a balanced position. They said the PLO sought Egypt's help in order to create a balance.
The prime minister's office said Netanyahu's aide Dore Gold would visit Cairo on Wednesday for talks with Egyptian officials.
The Israeli official said that Gold's visit was intended to "put off the visit by Moussa here (in Israel) and instead to hold talks between advisers on the two sides."
